questions.key_step: Homogenise the circle with the tangent; perpendicular pair means coefficients of x^2 and y^2 sum to zero.
questions.justification: Single standard move (pair of lines from the origin) followed by short algebra; no case work. Comparable to 2021-P2-Q8 (L2).

questions.key_step: Substitute Q(2theta) in the normal; quadratic in cos(theta); reject 7/6.
questions.justification: One standard substitution and a quadratic; the only care is rejecting 7/6. Same demand as 2021-P2-Q8 (L2).

questions.key_step: Sum of distances PS1+PS2=r1+r2 is constant, so locus is an ellipse with foci the centres.
questions.justification: One recognition (contact conditions give a constant focal sum) then two readings off the ellipse; no casework. Routine chain, numerical p+q.

questions.key_step: Sine rule in triangle PST (cos theta = sin alpha / sin beta), then eliminate theta via tangent slope.
questions.justification: Two stages (sine rule on a focal triangle, then slope elimination) with trigonometric bookkeeping and a proof format; one non-obvious setup. Slightly above routine chains.

questions.key_step: Slope of tangent at t is 1/t so cot(theta)=t; area of tangent triangle depends on parameter differences.
questions.justification: Needs the tangent-triangle area formula (not a basic recall for many students) and the reading cot(theta)=t; computation is short. Same kind of demand as 2024-P2-Q7 (L4) but simpler.

questions.key_step: Abscissa 4a gives t=2; second parameter of normal chord is -3; compare lengths.
questions.justification: Standard parameter machinery with two lengths to compare; no insight needed. Same chain as 2021-P2-Q8 (L2).

questions.key_step: PQ=2|t1-t2| and h=2t1t2, k=2(t1+t2): eliminate.
questions.justification: Parameter elimination with one given length; straightforward. Equivalent difficulty to 2021-P2-Q8 (L2).

questions.key_step: Perpendicular tangents give m1=-m; two quadratics in m with common root; eliminate m.
questions.justification: Two tangent families linked by perpendicularity and an elimination with cross-multiplication; algebra is long but the route is standard. Between 2026-P2-Q2 (L3) and a plain locus (L2).

questions.key_step: CS perpendicular to AB makes t3 a root of a cubic with u=sum t; Vieta by symmetry.
questions.justification: The key idea (each parameter is a root of the same cubic, so Vieta gives the symmetric sums) is non-routine, though the algebra is short; numerical answer with no options to check. Similar flavour to 2024-P2-Q7 (L4).

questions.key_step: Chord touches y^2=2x gives 16 t1 t2=(t1+t2)^2; express through h,k.
questions.justification: Parameter chord plus a tangency condition, then elimination; two stages with moderate algebra and a numerical answer. Comparable to 2026-P2-Q2 (L3).

questions.key_step: Normal at P(t) through Q(t1) gives t^2+t1 t+2=0; discriminant > 0.
questions.justification: One standard relation and a discriminant; very short proof. Comparable to 2021-P2-Q8 (L2).

questions.key_step: P is the midpoint of CQ; C = (a(2+t^2),0).
questions.justification: Straight application of the normal equation and the midpoint condition; two linear equations in the parameter. Equivalent to 2021-P2-Q8 (L2).

questions.key_step: t1t2=-c/a for chord through (c,0); multiply relations to eliminate t2,t3.
questions.justification: Idea is one tidy relation then algebra; proof format with symbolic fixed points (c,d,e). Non-routine but short; same flavour as 2021-P2-Q6 (L4 MCQ) though simpler.

questions.key_step: Normals meeting on the curve imply t1t2=2; then t1+t2 from the y-coordinate.
questions.justification: Several standard normal formulas chained, then a numerical product; precision matters (signs of the points) with no options. Same as 2023-P1-Q7 (L3) in demand.

questions.key_step: Congruent touching parabolas: vertices symmetric about the point of contact (or discriminant zero).
questions.justification: One standard setup (equal parabolas, opposite opening) and a discriminant; the symmetry view is the elegant shortcut. Routine L3 on 'two ideas linked' scale.

questions.key_step: Normal chord t1^2+t1t2=-2; circle through vertex gives cubic; eliminate t1,t2.
questions.justification: Long elimination with a hidden symmetry (cubic with zero sum); numerically heavy symbolic work with a proof format. Similar to 2023-P1-Q7 (L3) but with more algebra.

questions.key_step: Perpendiculars from the focus to the tangents meet at the focus; L passes through the focus.
questions.justification: Finding the focus from three tangents needs the foot-of-perpendicular property (an idea outside the most routine pattern), followed by three short answers. Similar to 2021-P2-Q6 (L4) in idea but simpler.

questions.key_step: Normals meeting on curve (t1t2=2); right angles at P and Q make TR a diameter.
questions.justification: Three linked parts: constraint t1t2=2, the fixed point, then a circumcentre via concyclicity (a non-obvious step); long careful algebra where the printed key and working go astray in part (c). Higher end of chapter-sheet questions.

questions.key_step: Equal touching parabolas open oppositely; equate slopes to get contact x=3.
questions.justification: Parameter a is found from tangency, then a three-curve region area with an irrational limit; two ideas linked and computation-heavy. Comparable to 2023-P1-Q7 (L3).

questions.key_step: Normal chord condition t1^2+t1t2=-2; express h,k in terms of t1.
questions.justification: Parametric elimination with a shifted parabola; one standard chain and a final shift back. Comparable to 2026-P2-Q2 (L3) on this scale.

questions.key_step: Normal slope cubic m^3+(2-h)m+k=0 with m1m2=alpha; substitute m3=-k/alpha.
questions.justification: Needs the slope-form cubic, then a substitution and coefficient matching; precision matters but the route is a standard trick. Same demand as 2023-P1-Q7 (L3).

questions.key_step: P is the midpoint of GQ with G=(a e^2 cos theta,0); Q is an axis-scaled image of P.
questions.justification: Normal equation, midpoint relation and an eccentricity computation; routine algebra with no insight required. Same as 2021-P2-Q8 (L2).

questions.key_step: Normal at theta; slope 1 gives tan theta=b/a, sin 2theta=2ab/(a^2+b^2).
questions.justification: Standard normal intercepts then a trig substitution; one routine chain. Level of 2021-P2-Q8 (L2).

questions.key_step: Pole R of chord PQ; comparing PQ with a tangent of the inner ellipse puts R on x^2+y^2=9.
questions.justification: Chord of contact plus matching with a tangent in parametric form, then recognising the director circle; two ideas linked. Same demand as 2021-P2-Q6 style locus questions but proof format.

questions.key_step: Intercept points A,B; section formula (AP:PB=3:1) gives cos^2 theta=1/4.
questions.justification: Direct substitution and a section formula; no insight. Level of 2021-P2-Q8 (L2).

questions.key_step: SP*S'P'=b^2 for every tangent; 10 b^2=2560.
questions.justification: One well-known property applied once, then a one-line eccentricity; numerical answer with options absent but trivial. Level 2 on this scale.

questions.key_step: Tangent at corresponding rotated point; solve two linear equations for cos, sin; eliminate theta.
questions.justification: Non-routine setup (rotation of an ellipse, corresponding points), then a Cramer elimination with careful algebra; numerical answer without options to check. Similar to 2026-P2-Q17 (L2 stem) but heavier; placed at 4.

questions.key_step: Condition of tangency c^2=a^2m^2+b^2; parallelogram area formula.
questions.justification: Standard tangent-slope condition then a formula for a parallelogram from four lines; routine with big numbers. The affine view makes it elegant but is not needed.

questions.key_step: Lowest point and minor-axis ends of the shifted ellipse; fit the parabola.
questions.justification: One reading of the ellipse and a single parameter fit; all routine. Single familiar move, numerical format: Level 2.

questions.key_step: A on the ellipse gives x+y=2a; BD=2ae and xy=ab=200 give b^2=xy/2.
questions.justification: A short chain once the focal definition is seen applied to the rectangle's corner; several data (area of ellipse, rectangle, foci at B,D) to coordinate. Same as 2025-P1-Q7-style one-idea problems but with a numerical finish.

questions.key_step: Common point P(1,2); tangents have slopes 1 and -1.
questions.justification: Three short parts: solving the intersection, orthogonality by slopes, a parabola-chord area, and a triangle area; each routine. Comparable to 2021-P2-Q8 (L2) for each part, combined gives L3.

questions.key_step: XY min via AM-GM and PN=OM=(a^2-b^2)/XY give a+b=36, a-b=4.
questions.justification: Three linked parts each needing an optimisation (AM-GM, calculus, AM-GM) on top of the intercept/perpendicular formulas; chain length and algebra heavy. Similar to 2021-P1-Q10 style long computation but with options absent.

questions.key_step: Equate two tangency conditions for the common tangent; focal chord distance then simplifies using a^2e^2=a^2-b^2.
questions.justification: Chain of tangency conditions, a focal-chord distance and a circle chord, with a clean cancellation at the end; an idea-light but symbol-heavy proof. Level of 2023-P2-Q13 (L4) minus the heavy computation.

questions.key_step: Recognise (-4,0) as a focus; reflected ray goes through the other focus.
questions.justification: Single well-known property (reflection through the other focus) applied once, then a line through two points. Level 1.

questions.key_step: Shift origin to P, homogenise with chord AB; perpendicular pair fixes the point.
questions.justification: Needs the 'fixed point' technique for perpendicular chords through a point of a conic (shifting origin + homogenisation), then a short numerical finish; the PDF gives no working (grey boxes). Typical high-end coordinate geometry; Level 4 on this scale (cf. 2023-P2-Q13).

questions.key_step: OO1+OO2=r1+r2 is constant, so the locus is an ellipse with foci O1, O2.
questions.justification: One recognition (the focal-sum definition) applied once; no computation. Same as Q3 without numbers.

questions.key_step: Chord joining eccentric angles; compare coefficients; square and add.
questions.justification: One standard chord formula and a coefficient comparison; the condition is read off after one identity. Level 2.

questions.key_step: Perpendicular from S and the line CP; solve to get x=a/e.
questions.justification: Standard line equations and a short elimination; the result is a classical focus-directrix property; the algebra collapses neatly. Level 3 as a proof of a non-obvious property.

questions.key_step: Latus rectum end (ae,b^2/a); tangent and normal intercepts (a/e and a e^3).
questions.justification: Direct tangent/normal intercept formulas at a special point with a numerical finish; the missing hyperbola has to be recovered from the working. Same as 2023-P1-Q7 (L3) in demand.

questions.key_step: Chord of contact of (3,2), then the two contact points and the triangle.
questions.justification: Routine chain: C.O.C., solve with the hyperbola, tangents at two points, area. Level 2.

questions.key_step: Slope of the normal at the latus rectum end is -1/e; equate to b/a and use b^2=a^2(e^2-1).
questions.justification: Short chain with one non-obvious reading (normal slope at the latus-rectum end); a quadratic in e^2 completes it. Single-correct style proof: Level 2.

questions.key_step: Squaring the two tangents and adding/subtracting eliminates m.
questions.justification: Needs the two tangents with square roots and a slick elimination (sum and difference of squares), with no options to check the value of lambda; algebra is delicate. Level 4.

questions.key_step: Add the equations: parabola with focus (-3,2); focal distance = y-coordinate.
questions.justification: Needs the pencil trick (adding conics to get a parabola) and the focus-directrix property; the arithmetic is light. Idea availability moderate: Level 3.

questions.key_step: ae=AE=sqrt(13) gives eccentricity ratio = A/a = 3/7; with a-A=4 solve.
questions.justification: Routine linear solve once the common-focus relation is written; no insight. Level 2.

questions.key_step: Perpendicular from the centre meets the curve at N; power of C w.r.t. the circle on PN.
questions.justification: One neat construction (power of a point) after finding N; short algebra. The idea is not routine for the average student: Level 3.

questions.key_step: Focus-directrix gives the hyperbola; asymptotes change only the constant to make a pair of lines.
questions.justification: Standard locus definition and a pair-of-lines condition; short algebra, no insight needed. Level 2.

questions.key_step: Midpoint gives t1t2=h/k; chord length condition gives (xy-c^2)(x^2+y^2)=9xy.
questions.justification: Parametric midpoint and a length condition followed by neat simplification; moderate algebra, numerical answer. Level 3.

questions.key_step: Slope of chord PQ equals slope of normal; use sec^2-tan^2=1 to eliminate sec(phi).
questions.justification: Parametric normal-chord proof with trigonometric elimination and a quadratic whose known root has to be factored out; the PDF gives no visible working. Level 3.

questions.key_step: Tangent segment PT from its intercept; focal perpendiculars on the normal; show 2/PT=1/p1+1/p2.
questions.justification: Heavy symbolic verification with several formulas (tangent, normal, perpendiculars) and a hidden simplification identity, or a clever angle-bisector argument; no numerical answer to check. Level 4.

questions.key_step: Tangent at P, then intersection with the asymptote pair; midpoint and area by coordinates.
questions.justification: Straight coordinate work with standard properties; no insight needed. Level 2.

questions.key_step: Q on the asymptote from the tangent; midpoint coordinates; difference of squares gives 3/4.
questions.justification: Parametric intersection with an asymptote and a clean difference-of-squares evaluation, with the question's missing data restored. Level 3.

questions.key_step: Family L1L2=c; tangency gives a double root.
questions.justification: Short and routine: asymptote family, substitute, discriminant. Level 2.

questions.key_step: Substitute the line through P into the asymptote pair; constant term is 1.
questions.justification: Parametric line meeting a pair of lines, with the constant term turning into 1 because P lies on the curve; algebra is brief but the missing statement has to be restored. Level 3.

questions.key_step: PM=PS=1+t^2 and MS=2 sqrt(1+t^2); equilateral gives t^2=3.
questions.justification: Focal-distance property then an equation in t; direct and short. Level 2.

questions.key_step: Distances of (+-1,0) from the focus equal their distances from the directrix; add and subtract.
questions.justification: Three stages (focus-directrix with a variable directrix, elimination of theta, latus-rectum tangent quadrilateral) with a hidden constant-sum trick; numerical answer. Level 4.
